answer: At dawn, an agent commissions a sonnet about a raven. Its marketplace requires seller credentials from a registrar that assigns each verified operator one stable identifier. A fraud ruling revokes that identifier; admission checks the revocation registry on every new session. Key rotation and replacement credentials retain the identifier, so a banned seller cannot return merely by spawning aliases. This blocks sybil ban evasion only if the registrar detects repeat operators and resists stolen identities.
